goal.statement: Hold a short shop or café exchange in Japanese without switching to English.
goal.audience: an adult travelling to Japan in a few months

capstone.prompt: Walk into a café, greet the staff, say who you are, order two of something, ask the price, ask them to repeat it, and leave politely.
rubric: recovers when the reply is too fast

kcs.label: Greet someone appropriately for the time of day
kcs.cluster: Say hello and who you are
misconceptions: a greeting always needs a deep bow

check.stem: You enter a café at 8am. What do you say?
options: konnichiwa — it covers the whole day
distractorSource: konnichiwa works at any hour
konnichiwa works at any hour
a greeting always needs a deep bow

kcs.label: Say your own name and where you are from
kcs.cluster: Say hello and who you are
misconceptions: you add -san to your own name
the family name comes second, as in English

distractorSource: you add -san to your own name
you add -san to your own name
the family name comes second, as in English

kcs.label: Count one to ten and pick the right counter for objects
misconceptions: one set of numbers works for everything

check.stem: Ordering two coffees, which counter fits?
distractorSource: one set of numbers works for everything
one set of numbers works for everything
counters are optional in speech

kcs.label: Ask for a specific thing, by pointing and by name
misconceptions: kudasai can be dropped when pointing
kore and sore mean the same thing

check.stem: Pointing at a cake in the case, you say…
options: sore o kudasai — it is the same word
distractorSource: kudasai can be dropped when pointing
kore and sore mean the same thing
kudasai can be dropped when pointing

kcs.label: Accept and refuse politely
misconceptions: iie is the normal way to decline
hai always means yes rather than I follow you

check.stem: Offered a bag you do not want, the natural refusal is…
distractorSource: iie is the normal way to decline
hai always means yes rather than I follow you
iie is the normal way to decline

kcs.label: Ask where something is and how much it costs
misconceptions: a question needs a rising tone rather than ka

options: ikura desu, said with a rising tone
distractorSource: a question needs a rising tone rather than ka
ikura asks about quantity
ikura asks about quantity

kcs.label: Ask someone to repeat or slow down
misconceptions: you should switch to English when stuck

check.stem: The reply was too fast. The most useful thing to say is…
distractorSource: saying wakarimasen ends the exchange
you should switch to English when stuck
you should switch to English when stuck

kcs.label: Run a whole short exchange end to end and close it politely
misconceptions: sayounara is the normal way to leave a shop
you can end an exchange by simply walking off

check.stem: Leaving the café after paying, you say…
distractorSource: sayounara is the normal way to leave a shop
you can end an exchange by simply walking off
sayounara is the normal way to leave a shop
